clue.text: Cain-like character's awful black stare (5, )

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: awful says the letters of black stare are in a terrible state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A villain resembling Cain fixes someone with a dreadful dark glare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges BLACK STARE. Caleb Trask is the younger brother in Steinbeck's East of Eden, a retelling of the Cain and Abel story.
explanation.definitionFit: Steinbeck modelled the jealous brother in East of Eden on the Biblical Cain, so he is a Cain figure.

clue.text: One hacking in Chiba could be a patient

definitions.meaning: the hacker hero of William Gibson's Neuromancer works the streets of Chiba City
doctors refer to someone under their care as a ...

explanation.surface: A computer intruder in Japan might turn out to be someone in a doctor's care.
explanation.walkthrough: Case is the console cowboy of Gibson's Neuromancer, which opens in Chiba City; 'could be' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neuromancer protagonist is named Case, and a medical case is a person being treated.

clue.text: Continue to tell tales on radio in Jad-bal-ja?

indicators.note: broadcasting means the words are heard rather than read, so the phrase is taken as spoken

parts.note: to keep telling lies is to lie on

explanation.surface: Someone keeps spinning yarns over the airwaves about an exotic name.
explanation.walkthrough: Jad-bal-ja is Tarzan's golden lion in Edgar Rice Burroughs's books; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Tarzan stories Jad-bal-ja is the ape-man's faithful golden big cat, an example of the species.

clue.text: The two who finally will meet Waltz King writer ()

parts.note: both means the two together

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of who

parts.note: Johann Strauss II was nicknamed the Waltz King

explanation.surface: A pair will at last be introduced to the famous Viennese composer's biographer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will meet' simply joins the pieces. Botho Strauss is a German playwright and novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Botho Strauss is a contemporary German dramatist and essayist, so he is a man of letters.

clue.text: Give new title to opening run after review

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: after review is read as once looked back over, so the word for opening is turned round

parts.note: a gate is an opening in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: A theatre renames a show's first night following a critic's notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after review' is read as 'once looked back over', so the opening is turned round. 'Opening run' pretends to be a show's first performances.
explanation.definitionFit: To tag is to label, so to label afresh is to rename.

clue.text: American turned on Republican associated with late beat

indicators.note: turned means the short word for American faces the other way

parts.note: the late person has died, that is passed away

explanation.surface: A US citizen went for a Republican linked with a dead Beat writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives SU. 'Late beat' looks like a reference to the Beat Generation; 'beat' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat a rival is to outdo or exceed them.

clue.text: Comic describing liberal assistant lecturer

indicators.note: describing is used in its sense of drawing round, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a wit is a comic, a joker

explanation.surface: A stand-up portrays a left-leaning junior university teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Wilt, hero of Tom Sharpe's comic novel Wilt, is an assistant lecturer in Liberal Studies, so the surface is the book itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Sharpe's hapless Henry Wilt teaches as a junior member of college staff.

clue.text: Chap who wrote of Animal Inn is a hard criminal (5, )

indicators.note: criminal says the letters are crooked and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: An author describes a pub where beasts gather as a tough lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges INN IS A HARD. Indra Sinha's novel Animal's People is narrated by a boy called Animal; the clue's 'Animal Inn' is a false phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Indra Sinha wrote Animal's People, whose narrator is the crippled boy called Animal.

clue.text: Coming across a piece of Breckinridge-like poetry?

parts.note: Myra Breckinridge, Gore Vidal's heroine, is a transgender woman, so trans
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Stumbling on a fragment of poems in the style of a Gore Vidal heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a piece of' joins the pieces. Gore Vidal's Myra Breckinridge has a heroine who has changed sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transverse lies crosswise, running from one side to the other.

clue.text: Spirits conservative gets Harrison Bergeron? (5, )

parts.note: shorts are spirits served in small measures
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A right-winger is handed drinks named after a Vonnegut character.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrison Bergeron is a Kurt Vonnegut piece of short fiction; the question mark marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Vonnegut's Harrison Bergeron is a brief prose fiction, one example of the form.

clue.text: News chief with article about "woke" Pontellier

parts.note: ED, editor, is the chief at a newspaper

indicators.note: about means the article is turned around

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An editor writes a piece on a fashionably progressive figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AN into NA. Edna Pontellier is the heroine of Kate Chopin's The Awakening, hence 'woke'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate Chopin's The Awakening follows Edna Pontellier's gradual awakening, so she is the one who woke.

clue.text: Idle Humans or novel like The Thin Man?

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Lazy people, or perhaps a Dashiell Hammett crime story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges IDLE HUMANS OR. The Thin Man looks like Hammett's novel, but is read as a scrawny man.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who is very thin may be underfed, lacking proper nourishment.

clue.text: "The ships hung in the sky in much the same way that bricks don't" (-)

definitions.text: "The ships hung in the sky in much the same way that bricks don't"

parts.words: "The ships hung in the sky in much the same way that bricks don't"
parts.note: a famous line from The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, describing the alien fleet; the solver names its author

explanation.surface: A quotation about spaceships hovering impossibly, unlike bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: The line comes from The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, written by this comic science-fiction author.

clue.text: "It's only because of their stupidity that they're able to be so sure of themselves" ()

definitions.text: "It's only because of their stupidity that they're able to be so sure of themselves"

parts.words: "It's only because of their stupidity that they're able to be so sure of themselves"
parts.note: a line from The Trial; the solver names the Prague writer who wrote it

explanation.surface: A quotation scorning the confidence of fools.
explanation.definitionFit: The remark is spoken in The Trial, the novel by this Prague-born German-language writer.

clue.text: You might say Dante's Inferno let loose

definitions.note: possessive standing for an adjective: belonging to Dante, a native of Florence

indicators.note: let loose says the letters are freed to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes Dante's vision of Hell being unleashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You might say' merely links. 'let loose' rearranges INFERNO LET.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante was born in Florence, so anything of his is of that city.

clue.text: It could be those like the Bronte sisters

definitions.meaning: it is slang for sex, as in sexual intercourse
Charlotte, Emily and Anne were siblings, family members to one another

explanation.surface: A remark that something might be what the Bronte sisters were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' links the two senses. 'It' for sex is an old euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexual intercourse is politely called relations, and family members are also relations.

clue.text: Where one finds broken white lines in a book

definitions.text: Where one finds broken white lines
definitions.meaning: dashed white markings are painted along the middle of a highway

explanation.surface: A place to find interrupted white lines inside a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links the two senses. 'broken white lines' suggests verse on a page, but means road markings.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashed lane markings are painted on highways, and Kerouac's novel has this title.

clue.text: Lengthy section of Cyrano De Bergerac about one row

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the nose goes around the next piece

parts.words: Lengthy section of Cyrano De Bergerac
parts.note: Cyrano is famous for his enormous nose
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A long passage of Rostand's play deals with a single line of seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lengthy section' suggests a long speech, but it is Cyrano's long nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A row is a din or racket, loud sound.

clue.text: Major love of mother by northern men

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are the men in the army
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A senior officer's affection for his mother, beside soldiers from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'by' join the pieces. Norma Major is the wife of John Major, British prime minister 1990 to 1997.
explanation.definitionFit: John Major's wife is called Norma, so she is his beloved.

clue.text: Man of the Elmet Trust announced tough cuts

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British young tough

indicators.note: announced means the next word is spoken, so its sound matters

parts.note: hews means cuts, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A heritage trust declares severe spending reductions.
explanation.walkthrough: Remains of Elmet is a Ted Hughes poetry collection, and the Elmet Trust promotes his work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elmet Trust celebrates the poet laureate whose collection Remains of Elmet is named after the old Yorkshire kingdom.

clue.text: My genial kiss excited author Robert Markham (4)

indicators.note: excited says the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A friendly passionate embrace thrills a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Markham was the pen name under which Kingsley Amis wrote the James Bond novel Colonel Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley Amis published Colonel Sun under the pseudonym Robert Markham.

clue.text: Some had it in for a goddess

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people bore a grudge against a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for a goddess' as definition; 'for' is a link word, so the definition is 'a goddess'. 'had it in for' pretends to be the idiom for a grudge.
explanation.definitionFit: Aditi is the Vedic mother of the gods in Hindu mythology.

clue.text: Woman whose lover drowned man on river close to Ohio

parts.note: he is a male person

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A grieving woman whose sweetheart drowned in an American river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the pieces. In Greek myth Leander drowned swimming the Hellespont to his beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Greek legend the priestess loved Leander, who drowned crossing the Hellespont to visit her.

clue.text: Twosomes lacking energy upset Tony Burg, perhaps

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards
lacking means the letter for energy is dropped

parts.note: duets are pieces for two
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Pairs running out of steam annoy a certain Tony Burg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' turns DUETS into DUTS, and 'upset' reads that upwards as STUD. 'perhaps' marks Tony Burg as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is slang for a virile, sexually successful man, of which the named character is given as an example.

clue.text: A weapon for one like Dr Watson

definitions.meaning: Watson sets off Holmes's brilliance by contrast

explanation.surface: Holmes's companion is described as needing a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencing sword has this name, and a companion who shows off a hero by contrast is too.

clue.text: People like Lem with time for editing?

parts.note: Stanislaw Lem was a Polish writer, so his compatriots are Polish men

explanation.surface: Asking whether Lem's compatriots get time for revision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'for' join the pieces. Polishment is a rare word for the act of polishing; editing is a polish of prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Editing smooths and refines a text, a polishing of it.

clue.text: A large kiss enthrals European Beethoven fan

indicators.note: enthrals means holding captive, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A big smooch captivates a continental music lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Alex, narrator of Burgess's A Clockwork Orange, adores 'Ludwig van'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Burgess's violent teenage narrator in A Clockwork Orange worships Ludwig van's Ninth Symphony.

clue.text: Dowdier don sadly a likely victim of murder (5, )

indicators.note: sadly says the letters are in a poor state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shabbier university teacher is unfortunately a probable murder target.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens died before finishing The Mystery of Edwin Drood, so whether its hero was killed is never settled; hence 'likely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's unfinished novel strongly implies its young hero was killed, but never confirms the crime.
